title: Annotatio IV §.VI: Ignatius to Smyrna — Eucharist is the Savior’s flesh; Theodoret still cites it
pass_a_gloss: IGNATIUS’s words are read in the Epistle to the Smyrnaeans, by which he affirms: that the Eucharist is the Flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ, which suffered for our sins, which the Father by His kindness raised. Which words are therefore by no means to be judged of weakened faith, nor still counted among Ignatius’s wretchedly interpolated surviving Writings, because Theodoret also in the fifth century commemorates them in the third Dialogue titled apathēs or Impassible.
pass_b_english: Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans: the Eucharist is the Flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ, which suffered for our sins and which the Father raised.
Not to be written off as weak faith or among interpolated Ignatian writings — Theodoret in the fifth century still cites them in Dialogue 3 (apathēs / Impassible).
source_text: IGNATII verba leguntur in Epistola ad Smyrenses, quibus affirmat: Eucharistiam esse Carnem Servatoris nostri Jesu Christi, quæ pro peccatis nostris passa est, quam Pater suâ benignitate suscitavit. Quæ verba proptereà fidei sublestæ neutiquam censenda, nec miserè interpolatis Ignatii superstitibus Scriptis adhuc, accensenda, quod illa etiam Seculo Vtô Theodoretus commemorat, Dialogo tertio apathēs seu impatibilis ditô.
